Include a Figure on a Landscape Page (PDF Only)

Source: R/include_landscape_figure.R
include_landscape_figure.Rd

For a Quarto or R Markdown chunk with `results = "asis"`. When the document is rendered to PDF the figure is placed on its own landscape page; in HTML, Word and other formats it is a normal figure and no LaTeX is written, so nothing leaks into the output.

Usage

include_landscape_figure(
  path,
  caption = NULL,
  label = NULL,
  width = "100%",
  environment = c("landscape", "blandscape"),
  format = NULL
)

Arguments

path

Path to the image file, relative to the document.

caption

Optional caption text. Square brackets in it are escaped.

label

Optional cross-reference id (for Quarto use a `"fig-"` prefix, for example `"fig-flow"`).

width

Image width as a percentage or length (default `"100%"`).

environment

`"landscape"` (default) or `"blandscape"`; see PDF requirements.

format

Output format override: `"latex"`, `"html"`, `"docx"` or `"other"`. By default it is read from knitr.

Value

A string of class `knit_asis` (printed by knitr as raw markdown); with `format = NULL` outside knitr the format is `"other"`.

PDF requirements

The default `environment = "landscape"` uses the `landscape` environment of the LaTeX package pdflscape, so the document must load that package (in Quarto, under `header-includes`). With `environment = "blandscape"` the figure is wrapped in a begin/end macro pair named blandscape and elandscape that your own preamble defines. The function does not add packages to your document.

Examples

cat(include_landscape_figure("fig/flow.png", caption = "Flow", label = "fig-flow", format = "latex"))
#> 
#> 
#> ```{=latex}
#> \begin{landscape}
#> ```
#> 
#> ![Flow](fig/flow.png){#fig-flow width="100%"}
#> 
#> ```{=latex}
#> \end{landscape}
#> ```
#> 
cat(include_landscape_figure("fig/flow.png", caption = "Flow", format = "html"))
#> 
#> 
#> ![Flow](fig/flow.png){width="100%"}
#>
